solution:
[Textbook misprint: the item labels run \((i)\) to \((x)\) but \((vii)\) is printed TWICE — once for Ketal and again for Imine — so there is no \((viii)\) and the ten terms carry only nine distinct labels. All ten terms are answered below in the printed order; only the labelling is broken.] (i) Cyanohydrin: the \(\alpha\)-hydroxynitrile obtained when \(\text{HCN}\) adds across a carbonyl group.
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}\)

(ii) Acetal: a gem-dialkoxy compound \(\text{RCH(OR')}_2\) formed when an aldehyde reacts with two equivalents of a monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry \(\text{HCl}\).
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + 2\,\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{dry HCl}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OC}_2\text{H}_5)_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)

(iii) Semicarbazone: the condensation product of a carbonyl compound with semicarbazide, containing \(\text{>C=N-NHCONH}_2\).
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{H}_2\text{N-NHCONH}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=N-NHCONH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)

(iv) Aldol: the \(\beta\)-hydroxy aldehyde (or \(\beta\)-hydroxy ketone) formed when two molecules of an aldehyde (or ketone) having at least one \(\alpha\)-hydrogen combine in the presence of dilute alkali.
\(2\,\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. NaOH}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO}\) (3-hydroxybutanal)

(v) Hemiacetal: the \(\text{RCH(OH)(OR')}\) compound formed by addition of ONE molecule of alcohol to an aldehyde.
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)(OC}_2\text{H}_5)\)

(vi) Oxime: the \(\text{>C=N-OH}\) compound formed from a carbonyl compound and hydroxylamine.
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{NH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=NOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)

(vii) Ketal: the gem-dialkoxy compound \(\text{R}_2\text{C(OR')}_2\) obtained from a KETONE and two equivalents of alcohol (or one equivalent of a diol, giving a cyclic ketal).
\(\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + 2\,\text{CH}_3\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{dry HCl}} (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C(OCH}_3)_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)

(viii) Imine: the \(\text{>C=N-R}\) compound formed when a carbonyl compound condenses with a primary amine.
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=N-CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)

(ix) 2,4-DNP-derivative: the 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone obtained from a carbonyl compound and 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine; it separates as an orange-red solid and is used to detect \(\text{>C=O}\).
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{H}_2\text{N-NH-C}_6\text{H}_3(\text{NO}_2)_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=N-NH-C}_6\text{H}_3(\text{NO}_2)_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)

(x) Schiff's base: the imine \(\text{>C=N-R}\) obtained specifically from a carbonyl compound and a primary amine (usually aromatic).
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO} + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH=N-C}_6\text{H}_5 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)
_note: The book prints the label '(vii)' twice, for Ketal and for Imine; the second is answered here as (viii), which is what the run to (x) requires.

solution:
The principal chain is chosen so that it contains the carbonyl (or carboxyl) carbon, and it is numbered to give that group the lowest locant.

(i) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}\): five carbons in the chain, \(\text{-CHO}\) is C-1, methyl at C-4.
4-Methylpentanal

(ii) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH(C}_2\text{H}_5)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}\): the six-carbon chain carrying the greater number of substituents is chosen; keto at C-3, ethyl at C-4, chloro at C-6.
6-Chloro-4-ethylhexan-3-one

(iii) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCHO}\): four carbons, double bond between C-2 and C-3.
But-2-enal

(iv) \(\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{COCH}_3\): five carbons with two keto groups at C-2 and C-4.
Pentane-2,4-dione

(v) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{C(CH}_3)_2\text{COCH}_3\): six carbons, keto at C-2, two methyls at C-3 and one at C-5.
3,3,5-Trimethylhexan-2-one

(vi) \((\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCH}_2\text{COOH}\): four carbons in the chain, \(\text{-COOH}\) is C-1, two methyls at C-3.
3,3-Dimethylbutanoic acid

(vii) \(\text{OHCC}_6\text{H}_4\text{CHO-}p\): a benzene ring with \(\text{-CHO}\) at the 1 and 4 positions.
Benzene-1,4-dicarbaldehyde

(i) 3-Methylbutanal: \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-CH}_2\text{-CHO}\)

(ii) \(p\)-Nitropropiophenone: propiophenone is \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3\), so
\(4\text{-O}_2\text{N-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-CO-CH}_2\text{CH}_3\)

(iii) \(p\)-Methylbenzaldehyde: \(4\text{-CH}_3\text{-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-CHO}\)

(iv) 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one: \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH-CO-CH}_3\)

(v) 4-Chloropentan-2-one: \(\text{CH}_3\text{-CO-CH}_2\text{-CHCl-CH}_3\)

(vi) 3-Bromo-4-phenylpentanoic acid: \(\text{HOOC-CH}_2\text{-CHBr-CH(C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{-CH}_3\)

(vii) \(p,p'\)-Dihydroxybenzophenone: \((4\text{-HO-C}_6\text{H}_4)_2\text{C=O}\), two benzene rings each bearing \(\text{-OH}\) para to the carbonyl.

(viii) Hex-2-en-4-ynoic acid: \(\text{HOOC-CH=CH-C}\equiv\text{C-CH}_3\)

(i) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CO(CH}_2)_4\text{CH}_3\): seven carbons, keto at C-2.
IUPAC: Heptan-2-one. Common: methyl \(n\)-pentyl ketone (methyl amyl ketone).

(ii) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CHO}\): six carbons, \(\text{-CHO}\) is C-1, methyl at C-2, bromo at C-4.
IUPAC: 4-Bromo-2-methylhexanal. Common: \(\gamma\)-bromo-\(\alpha\)-methylcaproaldehyde.

(iii) \(\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_5\text{CHO}\): seven carbons.
IUPAC: Heptanal. Common: \(n\)-heptaldehyde (oenanthaldehyde).

(iv) \(\text{Ph-CH=CH-CHO}\): three carbons, \(\text{-CHO}\) is C-1, double bond at C-2, phenyl at C-3.
IUPAC: 3-Phenylprop-2-enal. Common: cinnamaldehyde.

(v) A cyclopentane ring bearing \(\text{-CHO}\):
IUPAC: Cyclopentanecarbaldehyde. No common name in use.

(vi) \(\text{PhCOPh}\):
IUPAC: Diphenylmethanone. Common: benzophenone.

(i) 2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazone of benzaldehyde:
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CH=N-NH-C}_6\text{H}_3(\text{NO}_2)_2\) (the nitro groups at positions 2 and 4 of the second ring)

(ii) Cyclopropanone oxime: a cyclopropane ring in which one ring carbon carries \(\text{=N-OH}\).

(iii) Acetaldehyde dimethyl acetal: \(\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OCH}_3)_2\)

(iv) Semicarbazone of cyclobutanone: a cyclobutane ring in which one ring carbon carries \(\text{=N-NH-CO-NH}_2\).

(v) Ethylene ketal of hexan-3-one: the C-3 carbon of hexane is bonded to both oxygens of an \(\text{-O-CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{-O-}\) bridge, giving the five-membered 1,3-dioxolane ring
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-C(-OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{O-)-CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\), i.e. 2-ethyl-2-propyl-1,3-dioxolane.

(vi) Methyl hemiacetal of formaldehyde: \(\text{H}_2\text{C(OH)(OCH}_3)\) (methoxymethanol).

Cyclohexanecarbaldehyde is \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{-CHO}\), a cyclohexane ring bearing an aldehyde group.

(i) A Grignard reagent adds across the carbonyl group; hydrolysis of the alkoxide gives a secondary alcohol.
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{CHO} \xrightarrow[\text{then H}_3\text{O}^{+}]{\text{PhMgBr}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{-CH(OH)-C}_6\text{H}_5\) (cyclohexyl(phenyl)methanol)

(ii) Tollens' reagent oxidises the aldehyde and deposits a silver mirror.
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{[\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2]^{+}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{COO}^{-} + \text{Ag}\downarrow\); acidification gives cyclohexanecarboxylic acid.

(iii) Semicarbazide condenses at the carbonyl group (weak acid is the optimum catalyst).
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{-CH=N-NH-CO-NH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\) (the semicarbazone)

(iv) Excess alcohol with an acid catalyst converts the aldehyde into the acetal.
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{-CH(OC}_2\text{H}_5)_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\) (the diethyl acetal)

(v) Zinc amalgam with concentrated hydrochloric acid is the Clemmensen reduction; \(\text{>C=O}\) is reduced all the way to \(\text{>CH}_2\).
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{-CH}_3\) (methylcyclohexane)

An aldehyde or ketone with at least one \(\alpha\)-hydrogen undergoes ALDOL condensation; an aldehyde with NO \(\alpha\)-hydrogen undergoes the CANNIZZARO reaction with concentrated alkali; anything that is neither does not react.

(i) Methanal, \(\text{HCHO}\) - no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen: CANNIZZARO.
\(2\,\text{HCHO} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. NaOH}} \text{CH}_3\text{OH} + \text{HCOONa}\)

(ii) 2-Methylpentanal, \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CHO}\) - one \(\alpha\)-hydrogen: ALDOL.
Aldol: \(\text{OHC-C(CH}_3)(\text{C}_3\text{H}_7)\text{-CH(OH)-CH(CH}_3)\text{-C}_3\text{H}_7\), i.e. 3-hydroxy-2,4-dimethyl-2-propylheptanal. Note that after the addition the \(\alpha\)-carbon carries no hydrogen at all, so this aldol cannot lose water; the reaction stops at the \(\beta\)-hydroxy aldehyde.

(iii) Benzaldehyde, \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}\) - no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen: CANNIZZARO.
\(2\,\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. NaOH}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa}\)

(iv) Benzophenone, \((\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_2\text{CO}\) - a ketone with no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen, and the Cannizzaro reaction is confined to aldehydes: NEITHER.

(v) Cyclohexanone - has \(\alpha\)-hydrogens: ALDOL.
Aldol: 2-(1-hydroxycyclohexyl)cyclohexan-1-one; on heating with loss of water: 2-(cyclohex-1-en-1-yl)cyclohexan-1-one.

(vi) 1-Phenylpropanone (propiophenone), \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3\) - has \(\alpha\)-hydrogens on the \(\text{-CH}_2\text{-}\): ALDOL.
Aldol: \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO-CH(CH}_3)\text{-C(OH)(C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_3\); on dehydration: \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO-C(CH}_3)\text{=C(C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_3\).

(vii) Phenylacetaldehyde, \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}\) - has \(\alpha\)-hydrogens: ALDOL.
Aldol: \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{-CH(OH)-CH(C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{-CHO}\); on dehydration: \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{-CH=C(C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{-CHO}\) (2,4-diphenylbut-2-enal).

(viii) Butan-1-ol - an alcohol, not a carbonyl compound: NEITHER.

(ix) 2,2-Dimethylbutanal, \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(CH}_3)_2\text{CHO}\) - the \(\alpha\)-carbon is quaternary, so there is no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen: CANNIZZARO.
Products: 2,2-dimethylbutan-1-ol and sodium 2,2-dimethylbutanoate.

All three products come from the aldol of ethanal, so the first step is common.
\(2\,\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. NaOH}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO}\) (3-hydroxybutanal)

(i) Butane-1,3-diol: reduce the aldehyde group of the aldol, leaving the hydroxyl intact.
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\)

(ii) But-2-enal: heat the aldol so that it loses water (aldol condensation).
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow[-\text{H}_2\text{O}]{\Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH-CHO}\)

(iii) But-2-enoic acid: oxidise but-2-enal with a mild reagent that does not attack the carbon-carbon double bond.
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH-CHO} \xrightarrow{[\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2]^{+}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH-COO}^{-} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH-COOH}\)

Both propanal, \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}\), and butanal, \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}\), have \(\alpha\)-hydrogens, so either can supply the carbanion (nucleophile) and either can be attacked at its carbonyl carbon (electrophile). Four combinations are therefore possible, and each aldol loses water on warming to give the \(\alpha,\beta\)-unsaturated aldehyde.

1. Propanal as nucleophile, propanal as electrophile:
Aldol \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-CH(OH)-CH(CH}_3)\text{-CHO}\) (3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal)
\(\rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-CH=C(CH}_3)\text{-CHO}\) (2-methylpent-2-enal)

2. Propanal as nucleophile, butanal as electrophile:
Aldol \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{-CH(OH)-CH(CH}_3)\text{-CHO}\) (3-hydroxy-2-methylhexanal)
\(\rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{-CH=C(CH}_3)\text{-CHO}\) (2-methylhex-2-enal)

3. Butanal as nucleophile, propanal as electrophile:
Aldol \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-CH(OH)-CH(C}_2\text{H}_5)\text{-CHO}\) (2-ethyl-3-hydroxypentanal)
\(\rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-CH=C(C}_2\text{H}_5)\text{-CHO}\) (2-ethylpent-2-enal)

4. Butanal as nucleophile, butanal as electrophile:
Aldol \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{-CH(OH)-CH(C}_2\text{H}_5)\text{-CHO}\) (2-ethyl-3-hydroxyhexanal)
\(\rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{-CH=C(C}_2\text{H}_5)\text{-CHO}\) (2-ethylhex-2-enal)

In each pair the aldehyde whose \(\alpha\)-carbon forms the new carbon-carbon bond is the nucleophile; the one whose carbonyl carbon becomes the carbinol (and then the alkene) carbon is the electrophile.

Molecular formula \(\text{C}_9\text{H}_{10}\text{O}\); degree of unsaturation \(= \dfrac{2(9)+2-10}{2} = 5\), which accounts for a benzene ring (4) and one \(\text{>C=O}\) (1).

It forms a 2,4-DNP derivative, so it is an aldehyde or a ketone. It reduces Tollens' reagent, so it is an ALDEHYDE. It undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction, so it has NO \(\alpha\)-hydrogen, which means \(\text{-CHO}\) is attached directly to the ring. Vigorous oxidation gives 1,2-benzenedicarboxylic acid (phthalic acid), so the ring carries a second carbon-containing side chain ORTHO to the \(\text{-CHO}\), and that side chain is oxidised to \(\text{-COOH}\).

Subtracting \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\) (the disubstituted ring) and \(\text{CHO}\) from \(\text{C}_9\text{H}_{10}\text{O}\) leaves \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\), an ethyl group.

The compound is 2-ethylbenzaldehyde (\(o\)-ethylbenzaldehyde), a benzene ring bearing \(\text{-CHO}\) at C-1 and \(\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_3\) at C-2.

Check: \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{CHO})(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5) = \text{C}_9\text{H}_{10}\text{O}\) and vigorous oxidation converts both side chains to \(\text{-COOH}\), giving benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid.
